annotations.title: Make a dashboard from a spreadsheet

description: Turn a spreadsheet export (Excel or CSV, up to 10 MB) into an Every Number dashboard. Returns a read-only dashboard link and every number on it with its receipt: the definition, the rows it used, and the rows it left out with the reason. Fixed rules lay out the screen and a database counts every number; no AI reads the file. Send the file as file_url (a Google Sheet shared as 'Anyone with the link', a Dropbox link, or a file in a public GitHub repository) or as file_content (CSV text, or base64 for Excel) with file_name. No account needed. Anyone with the link can open the dashboard, and it is deleted 24 hours after upload unless the person saves it. Limits: 5 files per 10 minutes and 20 per day from one place.

content_encoding.description: How file_content is written. Default: base64 for .xlsx, .xlsm and .xls, text for everything else.

file.description: A file the person attached in ChatGPT. ChatGPT fills this in. Other assistants send file_url or file_content instead.

file_content.description: The file itself, up to 10 MB: CSV or TSV text as it is, or an Excel file encoded as base64. Send this or file_url.

file_name.description: The file's name with its extension, such as orders-october.csv or pipeline.xlsx. Needed with file_content. It also becomes the dashboard's title.

file_url.description: A link to the file: a Google Sheet shared as 'Anyone with the link', a Dropbox link, a file in a public GitHub repository or gist, or an Every Number sample such as https://everynumber.app/samples/tickets/tickets-export-2026-10-18.csv. Send this or file_content.

sheet.description: For an Excel file with several sheets, the name of the sheet to read. Default: the sheet with the most data.

name: make_dashboard_from_file

dashboard_url.description: The dashboard, read-only. Anyone with this link can open it until it's deleted.

decision.description: The question the screen is laid out to answer, picked by rules from the columns.

expires_at.description: When the dashboard and the rows we read are deleted, unless it's saved (ISO 8601).

findings.description: What this file says, in sentences filled from the numbers.

number.description: key of the number in numbers

headline.description: The numbers across the top of the dashboard.

number.description: key of the number in numbers

exact.description: The same number with more precision, when it differs.

checks.description: Checks the number passed (ok true) or should be read with (ok false).

data_through.description: The last date in the data (YYYY-MM-DD), if the file has dates.

definition.description: The rule behind the number, in plain English.

math.description: The arithmetic from the rows in the file to the number, one step per line.

receipt_id.description: The receipt's fingerprint. Same file and same definition give the same ID.

rows_left_out.description: Rows skipped on upload (totals, blanks) and rows the definition leaves out, each with the reason.

rows.description: Row numbers in the file, such as 'Rows 4, 17 and 3 more'.

rows_outside_definition.description: Rows the definition doesn't cover, such as other statuses.

value.description: The number as the dashboard shows it.

title: Make a dashboard from a spreadsheet
